source.pageTitle: AI Working Group - Presentations and Workshops - 2026-09 - DO All Learning
source.notes: The 01 - Foo template heading was intentionally excluded. The first 170 ideas are extracted from the Confluence page; ideas 171–200 are workshop additions created to reach the requested collection of 200 ideas.

interestingPrompts.title: Tailwind via CDN
interestingPrompts.prompt: Modify the existing app’s styling to use Tailwind CSS loaded from its CDN. Keep all current interactions and content working, preserve the single-HTML-file constraint, and only change the visual implementation where it improves consistency.
interestingPrompts.sourceText: Use Tailwind (from their CDN) to style the app

interestingPrompts.title: Animations
interestingPrompts.prompt: Modify the existing app to add purposeful animations to its key feedback moments and transitions. Keep the interactions understandable, avoid animation on every element, and respect prefers-reduced-motion.

interestingPrompts.title: Visual styles and effects
interestingPrompts.prompt: Modify the existing app’s visual design with a coherent style direction such as glassmorphism, a retro interface, or a steampunk treatment. Preserve readability, usable controls, and the current app behavior while making the style easy to see.
interestingPrompts.sourceText: Visual styles/effects (eg glassmorphism, steampunk look, ...) (to help them experiment visually)

interestingPrompts.title: Visual interactions
interestingPrompts.prompt: Modify the existing app to add one meaningful direct-manipulation interaction, such as drag and drop, collapse and expand, or a clearer component interaction. Keep an equivalent keyboard path and preserve the current workflow.
interestingPrompts.sourceText: Visual interactions (eg drag and drop, collapse/expand, ui component names, ...)

interestingPrompts.title: Visualizations
interestingPrompts.prompt: Modify the existing app to add one meaningful visualization of the app’s existing data using a simple chart, graph, plot, or canvas treatment. Include a short text alternative and do not invent misleading data.
interestingPrompts.sourceText: Visualizations they can add (eg charts, graphs, plots, infinite Canvas using <Canvas>, etc)

interestingPrompts.title: Code quality and security
interestingPrompts.prompt: Modify the existing app to improve its code quality and client-side safety: validate user input, handle empty and unexpected values, remove avoidable duplication, and add a small visible or console-based test checklist for the important interactions.
interestingPrompts.sourceText: Code quality/security related (eg how to add tests, how to execute those etc)

interestingPrompts.title: Fetch web data
interestingPrompts.prompt: Modify the existing app to optionally fetch a small, relevant piece of public web data such as an image, logo, icon, or example list. Add loading, error, and empty states, keep a useful local fallback, and do not introduce a backend.
interestingPrompts.sourceText: Fetching data from the web (eg find images, logos, icons, etc)

interestingPrompts.title: Use SVGs
interestingPrompts.prompt: Modify the existing app to add or replace a visual with an inline SVG that fits the app. Make the SVG responsive and accessible, and keep all existing content and interactions usable without the graphic.

interestingPrompts.title: Cross-tab communication
interestingPrompts.prompt: Modify the existing app so two open tabs or windows can share meaningful state using BroadcastChannel with a storage-event fallback. Show a small synchronisation status and keep the app usable when communication is unavailable.
interestingPrompts.sourceText: Means to make tabs/windows running the same app communicate

interestingPrompts.title: Make it yours
interestingPrompts.prompt: Modify the existing app with one original creative feature or visual twist that fits its purpose. Keep the change focused, explain the choice in the UI or a short note, and preserve the current behavior and constraints.

ideas.title: Your Face All Mixed Up
ideas.description: Webcam pictures + puzzle
features: Turn the picture into a puzzle and let users solve it
ideas.constraints: One HTML file; no backend, no build step
ideas.starterPrompt: "Create a single page html app with tailwind (cdn) that (1) has a button to take a picture with the webcam (2) splits the picture in n squares (configurable) (3) randomizes those squares (4) displays those on a grid (puzzle like) and hides the picture that was taken (so users can't cheat) (5) let's users move the squares around to solve the puzzle (6) shows confettis and a green border when reassembled the puzzle pieces
sourceEvolutions: add filters/effects once the puzzle is completed (user can apply any)
add a save button once the puzzle is completed
